# Company and news research

## Valuation snapshot (Yahoo Finance)
- INFY on NSE: price ₹1,146.5 (prev close ₹1,123.15); market cap ~₹4.64 lakh cr; trailing P/E 15.27, forward P/E 14.35; P/B 4.77; dividend yield 4.63%; ROE 29.95%; debt/equity 8.57; profit margin 16.2%; revenue growth 1.4%; 52-week range ₹980.4–₹1,728; 50-DMA ₹1,080.3, 200-DMA ₹1,195.1 (2026-10-29; tool:get_stock_info; figures computed by the agent from this tool's data)
- Analyst consensus per Yahoo: mean target ₹1,200.07, recommendation key 'buy', 42 analyst opinions (2026-10-29; tool:get_stock_info)

## Q2 FY27 results and guidance
- Q2 FY27 revenue $5,145 mn, +1.2% QoQ and +1.5% YoY in constant currency (acquisitions ~0.4% of sequential growth); H1 growth 1.9% cc. Management said growth was below its expectations, volumes softer and price increases lower than anticipated amid high competitive intensity (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)
- FY27 revenue guidance cut to 1–2% YoY cc; operating margin guidance unchanged at 20–22%. Q2 operating margin 21%, down 0.1% QoQ; effective tax rate expected 29–30% (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)
- Q2 EPS ₹19.32 (+8.7% YoY); H1 EPS ₹38.51 (+11.7%). Free cash flow $928 mn (113% of net profit); cash $4.7 bn, debt-free; DSO 64 days (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)
- Prior guidance was 1.5–3% (Business Today); this is a second consecutive cut, and includes an unchanged 170 bps contribution from acquisitions (2026-10-26; https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/infosys-share-price-highest-lowest-targets-post-q2-results-buy-hold-or-sell-563530-2026-10-26)
- AI revenue 10.5% of total revenue, +29% sequentially (8.2% in prior quarter) (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)

## Management commentary, deals, headcount
- Q2 large deal TCV $5.2 bn (19 deals, 62% net new), including a net-new $2 bn+ seven-year mega deal with a financial services client (transition from second half of Q4; expected to add over 1% growth in FY28 per CFO) and a $1 bn renewal. H1 large deals $8.8 bn, +28% YoY (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)
- CFO: client spending remains cautious (geopolitics, inflation, shifting tech priorities). Net headcount +~4,400 in quarter; ~13,000 freshers hired in H1 vs ~20,000 FY27 target; attrition 12.7%; wage hikes effective Oct 2026 with next phase Jan 2027; utilisation incl. trainees 85.4% (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)
- Margin walk: 70 bps headwind from post-sales customer support, 20 bps from acquisitions; offsets of 40 bps rupee depreciation, 20 bps Project Maximus, 20 bps working days; a terminated EURS programme in Q1 had a 40 bps impact (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)

## Corporate actions
- Board declared interim dividend of ₹26/share (+13% YoY vs ₹23 last year) with Q2 FY27 results (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)
- FY26 final dividend ₹25/share, record date June 10, 2026, paid June 25, 2026 (AGM June 23, 2026) (2026-06; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000018/exv99w06.htm)
- Acquisition of Stratus Global LLC (US insurance tech) agreed March 25, 2026 for up to $95 mn incl. earn-outs; completed April 21, 2026 (2026-04-21; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w10.htm)
- Company completed its largest-ever ₹18,000 crore buyback in Q3 FY26 (Oct–Dec 2025), outside the 6-month window (2026-01; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067491/000106749126000002/exv99w02.htm)

## Broker ratings and targets after Q2 FY27

Nomura Buy, target ₹1,300 (from ₹1,310); CLSA Hold ₹1,003 (from ₹976); Jefferies ₹1,140 (from ₹1,160); Citi ₹1,105 (from ₹1,030) (2026-10-26; https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/infosys-share-price-highest-lowest-targets-post-q2-results-buy-hold-or-sell-563530-2026-10-26)
- UBS Buy, target ₹1,415 (~23% upside from Friday close). HSBC Hold, target ₹1,110, saying guidance is at the lower end of peers and wage hikes may pressure H2 margins (2026-10-26; https://www.tradingview.com/news/moneycontrol:4721e7b4c094b:0-buy-or-sell-infosys-stock-after-q2-earnings-miss-guidance-cut-ubs-sees-23-upside-hsbc-flags-margin-pressure/)
- Antique Stock Broking: Hold, target ₹1,115 (14x 1HFY29E EPS); Q2 TCV of $5.2 bn was well ahead of its $4 bn estimate. Another broker valued at 16x FY28E EPS for ₹1,300 target (~13% upside) (2026-10-26; https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/infosys-shares-drop-4-on-q2-guidance-miss-check-what-analysts-recommend-126102600141_1.html)
- Headline: Infosys shares dropped ~4% after the Q2 guidance miss (2026-10-26; https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/infosys-shares-drop-4-on-q2-guidance-miss-check-what-analysts-recommend-126102600141_1.html)

# Macro and geopolitical research

## Company/sector: Infosys Q2 FY27 and guidance
- Infosys Q2 FY27 (reported 23 Oct 2026): net profit ₹7,823 cr (+6.2% YoY), revenue ₹49,244 cr (+10.7% YoY). Direction: guidance cut is negative for sentiment; rupee-driven reported growth is a partial offset. (2026-10-23; https://www.itechguides.com/infosys-q2-results-profit-rises-6-yoy-to-rs-7823-crore-company-cuts-fy27-revenue-guidance/)
- FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance cut to 1%-2% from 1.5%-3%. Operating margin guidance kept at 20%-22%. Q2 CC growth was 1.5% YoY and 1.2% QoQ. Q2 operating margin was 21.0%. (2026-10-23; https://www.itechguides.com/infosys-q2-results-profit-rises-6-yoy-to-rs-7823-crore-company-cuts-fy27-revenue-guidance/)
- CFO commentary on the call: client spending remains cautious, reflecting geopolitical tensions, inflationary pressures and shifting technology priorities. Revenue growth was below company expectations. AI-first revenue was 10.5% of revenue. Large deal wins were $5.2bn (62% net new). Free cash flow was $928m (113% of net profit). (2026-10-23; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)

## Global peers and sector read-through
- Cognizant Q3 2026 (29 Oct 2026): revenue $5.7bn, +4.6% YoY (+4.8% CC). Financial Services +12% YoY. FY26 CC growth guidance revised to 4.0%-4.4%, adjusted operating margin ~16.1%. Over 50% of its code is AI-assisted. Read-through: mildly positive for demand, especially BFSI, but Cognizant's growth is well above Infosys's guided 1-2%. (2026-10-29; https://investors.cognizant.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Cognizant-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)
- Cognizant's earlier FY26 guidance (as of 29 July 2026) was CC growth of 4.0%-5.5%, so the revised 4.0%-4.4% range narrows the top end downward. (2026-07-29; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001058290/000105829026000030/exhibit9936302026.htm)
- Indian peers' Q2 FY27 results were mixed. Tech Mahindra grew 7.2% CC. Wipro grew 0.6%. HCLTech raised the low end of its FY27 guidance to 2.5%-4.0%. TCS had $9.6bn TCV and a $3.1bn annualised AI run rate. Infosys's 1-2% guidance is at the weaker end of large caps. (2026-10-16; https://univest.in/blogs/tcs-vs-hcl-tech-vs-tech-mahindra-vs-wipro-which-it-stock-won-q2-results-2026-ai-revenue-deal-wins-compared)
- Nifty IT rose about 1% on 29 Oct 2026 after the Fed hold, in a session where Nifty 50 closed at 22,936.75 (+1.05%). (2026-10-29; https://english.publictv.in/sensex-surges-905-points-nifty-closes-1-05-pc-higher-as-fed-rate-pause-boosts-market-sentiment/)

## Currency (INR)
- The rupee hit a two-week low of about 95.37 per USD on 29 Oct 2026 (previous close 95.22). It was held up by RBI intervention, and a persistent bearish bias was noted. Direction for INFY: a weaker rupee lifts rupee revenue and margin (positive), but this is largely a translation benefit and does not change CC demand. (2026-10-29; https://www.business-standard.com/amp/finance/news/rupee-hits-2-week-low-on-sticky-dollar-bids-modest-intervention-cushions-126102900511_1.html)
- Reuters noted that a weaker rupee lifts IT firms' dollar earnings when converted into local currency. This mechanism was cited in Dec 2025 coverage of IT index gains. (2025-12-04; https://www.marketscreener.com/news/india-s-stock-benchmarks-snap-losing-run-ahead-of-rbi-rate-decision-ce7d51dfda80f12c)
- Foreign investors have pulled about $31bn out of Indian markets in 2026. Nifty is down about 12.6% YTD and Sensex about 13.4%. Direction: FPI outflows and weak market breadth are negative for INFY, which is an FPI-held ADR/large-cap, though IT is a relative defensive. (2026-10-29; https://www.ibtimes.com.au/indian-shares-rise-fed-rate-pause-adani-ports-1877570)

## Fed / US rates
- The Fed held its rate at 3.75%-4.00% on 28 Oct 2026 in a 10-2 vote, with the dissenters favouring a hike. The Fed said inflation remains elevated, and markets price a possible hike in December. Direction: a hawkish tilt is negative for US tech spending and valuations. It also pressures EM currencies, but a weaker INR is a partial positive for INFY. (2026-10-29; https://www.ibtimes.com.au/indian-shares-rise-fed-rate-pause-adani-ports-1877570)

## RBI policy and domestic inflation
- On 7 Oct 2026 the RBI MPC unanimously raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% (first hike since Feb 2023). It shifted the stance to 'calibrated tightening' and said rate cuts are off the table near term. Headline CPI is expected to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters. Direction: neutral to mildly negative for INFY directly, since it has net cash. It is negative for broad Indian market sentiment and valuations. (2026-10-07; https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/10/09/rbi-hikes-repo-rate-to-5-50-percent-october-2026/)
- HSBC expects another 25 bps RBI hike in December. The next MPC meeting is 2-4 December 2026. September CPI was 5.54% (August 4.83%). (2026-10-23; https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/rbi-mpc-meeting-live-rate-hike-in-focus-as-inflation-oil-rise-liveblog/2999124/1)
- September CPI was 5.54%, up from 4.83% in August. MPC minutes (released 21 Oct) show a 4-2 split on whether inflation is generalised. The RBI rejected all bids in a T-bill sale. (2026-10-23; https://battleias.com/current-affairs/2026-10-23-mpc-minutes-rbi-rate-setters-divided-on-whether-inflation-is-spreading-what-it-means/)
- The next MPC meeting is 2-4 December 2026. (2026-10-07; https://www.corplawupdates.in/updates/rbi-repo-rate-hike-5-50-percent-october-2026)

## Commodity / geopolitics (oil, West Asia)
- Brent was at about $114.28-114.50/bbl on 29 Oct 2026. It hit $116.72 on 23 Oct, the highest since Apr/Jun 2022-era levels per sources, and is up about 77% YoY. Drivers: Strait of Hormuz disruption, Houthi strikes on Saudi energy sites, and US-Iran tensions and talks. Direction for INFY: indirect. Oil is a direct cost to INFY only via travel/energy (small), but high oil raises India inflation, pressures INR and the RBI, and weighs on client budgets (negative for sentiment). Wage inflation is a bigger input cost than commodities. (2026-10-29; https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil)
- The WSJ reportedly said Washington told Gulf states to prepare for a short campaign against Iran after the 3 Nov US midterm vote. Brent fell from $116.72 (23 Oct) to $113.88 (27 Oct) on Tehran talks, then rose above $115 on 28 Oct. Event risk is high around 3 Nov. A de-escalation deal would be a positive for markets and a negative for oil. (2026-10-28; https://www.oilandgasmiddleeast.com/news/brent-crude-price-drivers)
- Hormuz traffic remains far below pre-war levels (about 18 transits on Monday vs 140 daily pre-war per Windward). The West Asia conflict began in February 2026. (2026-10-28; https://www.engine.online/news/middle-east-conflict-oil-trades-above-usd115-bbl-as-us-and-iran-trade-counter-accusations-8352)
- The Strait of Hormuz handled about 20% of global energy shipments before hostilities began in February 2026. (2026-10-28; https://menafn.com/1111876360/Crude-Oil-Prices-Surge-After-Strike-On-Saudi-Refinery)

## US government policy: visas, immigration, trade
- On 8 Oct 2026 the US suspended several companies from the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme used to sponsor H-1B workers for green cards. Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL are the most affected. Direction: negative (talent cost, retention, compliance risk). (2026-10-14; https://thediplomat.com/2026/10/indian-it-companies-are-in-trumps-crosshairs/)
- A $100,000 annual or one-time fee on new H-1B petitions took effect on 21 Sept 2025 (initially 12 months). Infosys fell 4.5% on the announcement. A Bloomberg-referenced study suggests Infosys would have paid the fee for over 10,400 workers on a hypothetical basis. A commentary note says an extension of the fee has been discussed. Estimates are that Indian IT already hires 70-80% of its US workforce locally. Direction: negative for incremental onsite staffing, with limited impact on the existing model. (2025-09-22; https://www.intellinews.com/us-fee-on-h-1b-visas-rattles-indian-tech-stocks-402343/)
- Commentary on an H-1B fee extension notes it could add hundreds of millions in costs on a hypothetical basis, for TCS, Infosys and Cognizant. The practical impact may be limited because 70-80% of the US workforce is hired locally. (2026-09; https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/h1b-fee-impact-indian-it-cmua0rizh000f2znt4pgnozcc)
- Indian citizens received over 70% of H-1B visas in 2024. The US-India trade deal had been stalled/strained, with 25% tariffs plus a 25% Russian-oil penalty on Indian goods as of Sept 2025. IT services were not directly tariffed, but Systematix flagged a threat to India's $190bn services exports from protectionism. (2025-09-23; https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/business/trumps-new-h-1b-firewall-expands-us-protectionism-against-india-threat-to-usd-190-bn-service-exports-report)

- Whether the H-1B $100k fee was extended beyond Sept 2026 was not verified from a primary source. Only secondary commentary.

## Last 3 months

**Price move**
- INFY returned −0.79% over 3 months vs −5.05% for NIFTYBEES, outperforming by ~4.3pp.
- Over 1 month it returned +14.28% vs +0.54% (tool:get_technicals).
- It retested the ₹980–1,000 floor: a Sep 29 intraday low of ₹980.4 and an Oct 7 close of ₹992. It then rallied ~15.6% to ₹1,146.5 by Oct 29.

**Key events**
- **9 Oct:** Nifty IT rose 3.4% after TCS's Q2 results. By 21 Oct it was ~13% above its 9 Oct close ([Univest](https://univest.in/blogs/infosys-tcs-to-hcl-tech-tectonic-rally-in-indian-it-stocks-but-experts-recommend-just-one-it-stock-to-buy-target-sl)).
- **23 Oct, Q2 FY27 results** ([SEC 6-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w05.htm)):
  - Revenue was $5,145 mn, +1.2% QoQ and +1.5% YoY in constant currency. Management said growth was below its expectations.
  - FY27 guidance was cut to 1–2% cc from 1.5–3%. This is the second consecutive cut and includes ~170 bps from acquisitions ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/infosys-share-price-highest-lowest-targets-post-q2-results-buy-hold-or-sell-563530-2026-10-26)).
  - Operating margin was 21%; margin guidance was held at 20–22%.
  - EPS was ₹19.32 (+8.7% YoY). Free cash flow was $928 mn (113% of net profit).
  - Large-deal TCV was $5.2 bn, including a net-new $2 bn+ seven-year financial-services deal.
  - AI revenue was 10.5% of total.
  - An interim dividend of ₹26 was declared (+13% YoY).
- **23 Oct trading:** the stock swung between ₹1,197.8 and ₹1,038.05 intraday on 33.0M shares, closing at ₹1,153.8.
- **26 Oct:** shares fell ~4% on the guidance miss ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/infosys-shares-drop-4-on-q2-guidance-miss-check-what-analysts-recommend-126102600141_1.html)).
- **Since then:** the stock closed ₹1,123.15 on Oct 28 and ₹1,146.5 on Oct 29.

**Why it moved: not established.** The dossier did not search for an INFY-specific catalyst behind the October rally or the Oct 23 swing.
- The timing coincides with the sector rally after TCS's results. Whether that sector move, or Infosys's own deal wins, drove the stock is unverified.
- The Oct 29 rise came on a day Nifty IT gained ~1% after the Fed hold ([Public TV](https://english.publictv.in/sensex-surges-905-points-nifty-closes-1-05-pc-higher-as-fed-rate-pause-boosts-market-sentiment/)).
